title: City of Phoenix amendments to the 2023 National Electrical Code (2024 PBCC)
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: Each amendment sheet states 'Adopted by City of Phoenix Ordinance G-7397 effective August 1, 2025'; City Council action date 06/18/2025 (p.2 and every amendment sheet).
Art. 100 'Building' redefined so townhouse units separated by fire walls, or by double walls / non-load-bearing common walls per the IRC, are separate buildings (p.1).

New Art. 100 definition 'Elevator Disconnect Room or Closet': where the elevator controller is in the hoistway, disconnects/OCPDs/lighting/receptacles go in a full-height-door room on the controller level, within 50 ft travel of the hoistway, accessed from the corridor, qualified persons only, with a label at the controller (p.1).

210.52(C)(2)/(3) (Home Builders Association proposal): island/peninsula countertops 24 in x 12 in or larger need at least one receptacle, and receptacles may again be mounted up to 12 in below a flat island/peninsula with no way to mount within 20 in above it; staff committee denied it but DAB, TI&P subcommittee and Council approved as submitted (pp.3-5; checkbox status read from rendered p.5).
210.52(G)(1): each attached garage, and each detached garage with power, needs at least one receptacle per vehicle bay mounted between 18 in and 5.5 ft above the floor (p.6).
New 215.25: townhouse feeders may serve only that unit and may not pass through, above, below or attach to another townhouse unit, regardless of ownership (p.7).
250.118(4) amended: EMT is an equipment grounding conductor only with an additional (wire-type) EGC (p.8).
310.12 amended to remove 208Y/120 V single-phase feeders; the 83% dwelling service/feeder sizing applies only to 120/240 V single-phase (pp.9-10).

312.5(C) Exception No. 2 rewritten for one- and two-family dwellings: NM cables may enter the back of a surface-mounted panel through a sealed nonflexible raceway sleeve (3 in max diameter, 3-24 in long) with fittings, cables secured within 8 in, sheath extending 2 in into the enclosure; 60% fill permitted (p.12).

334.10 amended: NM/NMC limited to one- and two-family dwellings (and their garages/storage buildings), dwelling units in multifamily of Types III-V, cable trays in those dwellings, and dwelling units in Types I/II within raceways; the general 'other structures Types III, IV, V' permission is deleted, i.e. no NM in commercial buildings (pp.14-15).

Art. 620 (620.6(B), 620.22, 620.23, 620.25(B), 620.51(C)(1)) amended to add the elevator disconnect room or closet as the location for elevator disconnects, OCPDs, lighting switch and GFCI receptacles (pp.16-22).
notes: Proposal-sheet format with justifications. Plain-text extraction LOSES strikethrough/underline (deleted vs added text) and the ACTION TAKEN checkbox states; consult the PDF for exact wording. Only 'approved' items appear in this packet (a separate 'nec-denied.pdf' exists on the Phoenix site but was not downloaded).

title: Phoenix Building Code (codes & ordinances web page)
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: Lists the 2023 NEC as part of the 2024 Phoenix Building Construction Code with a link to the Phoenix NEC amendments (2024 PBCC section).

Notice: Phoenix is deferring enforcement of 2023 NEC 210.8(F) Exception 2; full enforcement of the GFCI requirement for HVAC equipment takes effect March 1, 2027 (notice near the top of the code list).
2017 NEC with 2018 Phoenix amendments is listed under the prior 2018 PBCC (2018 PBCC section).
notes: Web page; the March 1, 2027 date is a forward-dated enforcement change to watch. Page does not name a next (2026 NEC) adoption.

title: Phoenix Construction Code History (TRT/DOC/00550, Rev. 08/25)
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: Current codes adopted effective August 1, 2025 by Ordinance G-7397 include the 2023 National Electrical Code (p.1).
Previous codes effective July 6, 2018 (Ordinance G-6463) included the 2017 NEC (p.1).
Earlier Phoenix NEC editions: 2011 NEC (with 2012 codes, effective July 1, 2013), 2008 NEC effective May 1, 2009, 2005 NEC effective July 1, 2007 (pp.1-2).
notes: Useful for determining which NEC applied to existing installations by date.

title: 2024 Phoenix Building Construction Code Implementation notice
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: 2024 PBCC adopted June 18, 2025 with an effective date of August 1, 2025; plans submitted for initial review from August 1, 2025 must comply (p.1).
The 2018 PBCC remained available for certain complete plans submitted through December 31, 2025; all plans submitted after December 31, 2025 must comply with the 2024 PBCC (p.1).
Standard plans approved under the 2018 PBCC remain in effect until July 31, 2026 (p.1).
notes: All transition windows have now passed (as of 2026-11-14), so the 2023 NEC with Phoenix amendments governs new work.

title: Phoenix amendments to 2024 IBC Chapter 1 (Administrative Provisions)
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: 101.4.8: the National Electrical Code, as amended, applies to electrical installations including alterations, repairs and replacement (p.6).

105.1: a permit is required to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert or replace any electrical system regulated by the code; annual permits are available to firms employing qualified tradespersons on their own premises (105.1.1) (p.18).

105.2 electrical permit exemptions (Phoenix list): cord-and-plug utilization equipment; repair/replacement of motors 50 HP or less, transformers 45 kVA or less, or fixed appliances of same type/rating in same location; repair/replacement in kind of switches, receptacles, contactors and controls rated 60 A or less (not a service disconnect); replacement in kind of breakers rated 125 A or less (not a service disconnect) or any fuse; sign electrodes/transformers same size; temporary lab/theater wiring; Class 2/3 circuits not essential for life safety; wiring inside non-building-service machinery (pp.20-21, rendered page checked: base IBC items struck, Phoenix items underlined).

110.3.10.1: electrical rough-in inspection required for all conduit/wiring before concealment, and a final inspection before energizing; replacement building service equipment serving occupied space may be operated if an inspection request is filed within 72 hours (p.45).
105.5: permits expire 24 months after issuance unless extended (p.27).

Section 118 Building Maintenance Registration: electrical work under it must be performed or supervised by a licensed electrical supervisor, who must be an AZ licensed contractor in the category or hold a current IAEI Electrical General or ICC Commercial Electrical Inspector certification (pp.65-66).
Section 119 Phoenix journeyman/apprentice licenses cover plumbing, gas fitting and mechanical work only; no electrical journeyman class is listed (pp.68-69).
notes: Text extraction loses strikethrough/underline; deleted base-code text appears inline with added text. Read the PDF for exact amended wording.

title: Electrical Submittal Requirements Interpretation (TRT/DOC/00574)
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: Issued August 2017, revised February 2026; references 2024 IBC 107.1, 2023 NEC and A.A.C. R4-30-302 (p.1).

AZ-registered electrical engineer must seal plans for: critical-care health care, over 600 V, classified (hazardous) locations except Art. 511/514, work over 400 A or available fault current over 22,000 A, life-safety alarm/signaling, and public works (p.1).

Non-registrants may prepare plans for work 200 A or less with AFC 10,000 A or less at 120/208 V 3-ph or 120/240 V 1-ph, or for a detached single-family dwelling at 200 A or less with AFC 22,000 A or less (p.2).
One-line diagram must identify the serving utility (APS or SRP) and use the utility's published AFC tables applied at the SES, without crediting service laterals/drops (p.2).
AFC calculations are required from the SES to the lowest-rated OCPD, including when adding new breakers or equipment; solar PV projects require a three-line diagram and equipment cut sheets (pp.2-3).
Minor electrical work may be permitted on description/diagram without full plans at the Building Official's discretion (p.3).

title: Phoenix Online Permits brochure
publisher: City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department
keyFacts: Online residential permits include Electrical Utility Clearance, Electrical Service Upgrade (up to 200 A) and Electric Meter Socket Replacement; online commercial permits include Electric Utility Clearance/No Work, Add or Extend Branch Circuit, Preventative Maintenance Electrical Shutdown and Repair Vandalized Electrical Equipment (p.2).
Online commercial minor-work permits are for applicants with licensed contractors; properties in historic districts or with unresolved non-permitted construction cases are not eligible (p.2).
Permits can be bought online at phoenix.gov/pdd/onlineservices and inspections scheduled when work is complete (p.2).

title: Residential Permit by Inspector (RPBI) Program brochure (TRT/DOC/00690)

Submittals need a one-line electrical diagram, load calculations and panel schedules if a sub-panel is installed (p.4).
A job-site meeting with the field inspector (inspection code 602) is required before construction; inspection line 602-495-0800 (p.8).

publisher: Maricopa County Planning and Development Department

title: A.R.S. 11-861 Adoption of codes by reference (counties)
publisher: Arizona State Legislature
keyFacts: A county board of supervisors that has adopted zoning may adopt and enforce a building code and related codes for unincorporated zoned areas (subsection A).
County codes are limited to a building, electrical, plumbing or mechanical code adopted by a national code organization or by the largest city in that county (subsection C.1).
notes: Supports the point that Arizona has no statewide electrical code for private construction; adoption is local (cities under their own authority, counties under this statute). No official single statement 'no statewide code' was retrieved.

title: A.R.S. 32-1121 Persons not required to be licensed (incl. handyman exemption)
publisher: Arizona State Legislature
keyFacts: Owner-builders improving their own property for their own occupancy (not for sale or rent) are exempt; sale or rent within one year of completion is prima facie evidence of intent to sell/rent (A.5).
The 'handyman' exemption covers casual or minor work under $1,000 total but does NOT apply when the work requires a local building permit or is part of a larger operation (A.14(a)-(b)).
Exemptions A.4, A.9 and A.14 do not apply to electrical work done in connection with fire safety installations such as hardwired or interconnected smoke alarms (D.1).

title: A.R.S. 32-1122 Qualifications for contractor license
publisher: Arizona State Legislature
keyFacts: The Registrar of Contractors classifies and qualifies applicants and establishes written examinations (A).

The license names a qualifying party, who must have at least four years of practical or management trade experience (two within the last ten years) in the type of work, with limited credit for technical training (E.1).
The qualifying party must pass a written trade exam taken within two years before application plus knowledge of Arizona building, safety, health and lien laws and ROC rules, if required (E.2).
The exam is waived only if the qualifying party has qualified a license in this state in the same classification within the preceding five years (F).
notes: Licensing is of the contracting business via a qualifying party; this statute does not create an individual journeyman/master electrician license. ROC classification scopes (R-11/C-11/CR-11) are in A.A.C. R4-9-102/103/104, which could not be retrieved (azroc.gov and apps.azsos.gov returned a Cloudflare challenge).

title: A.R.S. 32-1151 Engaging in contracting without license prohibited
publisher: Arizona State Legislature
keyFacts: It is unlawful to contract, bid or offer to act as a contractor without a contractor's license in good standing unless exempt (text).
Securing a permit or employing a person on a project is prima facie evidence of a contract (text).

publisher: Salt River Project

title: City of Tucson Amendments to the 2023 National Electric Code (Exhibit H)
publisher: City of Tucson Planning & Development Services
keyFacts: 210.5(C)(1) and 215.12(C)(1): mandatory conductor color code - 120/208 Y black/red/blue/white; 277/480 Y brown/orange/yellow/grey; 120/240 delta black/orange/red/white; not required in residential occupancies (p.1).
210.11(C)(5): dwelling dishwasher and garbage disposer may share one 20 A branch circuit (p.1).

225.31(B) Exception 5: for freestanding canopies, carports, towers and similar structures the disconnect may be elsewhere on the premises if within sight or lockable open, with a 250.122 bonding conductor (p.2).
230.70(B): service disconnect labels must be engraved or raised letters fastened by screws or rivets; plastic tape not acceptable (p.2).
310.15(B)(3): outdoor ambient temperature for ampacity correction shall be not less than 45 C (113 F) (p.2).
340.10(7): Type UF permitted in mortar joints of adobe construction where NM is permitted (p.2).
